answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The onyx multiplier is published, charged in bridge, and quill lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1077 identities would post 3222 proofs and burn roughly 58 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
